implemented_requirements.evidence: BudgetTrackerGUI._build_expenses_tab creates entry fields and add_expense() calls tracker.add_expense; tracker.add_expense creates an Expense and saves it.
BudgetTrackerGUI.delete_expense() calls tracker.remove_expense(expense_id) which removes the expense and persists the change.
BudgetTracker.get_expenses_sorted() returns expenses sorted by date; GUI refresh_expenses() populates a Treeview with that data.
BudgetTrackerGUI._build_savings_tab provides a form; add_goal() calls tracker.add_goal(name, target) which creates a SavingsGoal and saves it.
BudgetTrackerGUI.deposit() triggers _transaction('deposit') which calls tracker.deposit(goal.id, amount).
BudgetTrackerGUI.withdraw() triggers _transaction('withdraw') which calls tracker.withdraw(goal.id, amount).
JSONStorage.load() and JSONStorage.save() are used by BudgetTracker to read/write a JSON file.
visualizer.py provides Matplotlib figures; BudgetTrackerGUI.refresh_reports() embeds them, with a text fallback when Matplotlib is unavailable.
Visualizer.text_summary() and Tracker.summary() generate multi‑line summaries; GUI shows them when Matplotlib is missing.
main.py creates JSONStorage, BudgetTracker, Tk root and launches BudgetTrackerGUI.

critical_issues: budgettrackergui.py contains placeholder CATEGORIES = [...] and is not used; however gui.py provides the functional GUI, so this does not prevent execution.
No explicit unit tests are provided, but the code is self‑contained and runnable.
judge.summary: The submitted code implements a full budget‑tracking application with expense entry, savings‑goal management, persistent JSON storage, and visual/text reports. All core functionalities are present and wired together, and the program can be launched via main.py. Minor redundancy (an unused budgettrackergui.py) does not affect operability, so the solution meets the benchmark.
